info.description: The Cavea server's REST API. JSON bodies with `snake_case` fields; times are RFC 3339 UTC. Routes under `/v1` that take a secret key also take a console session (the cookie `/console/api/session` sets): the request names its workspace in `Cavea-Workspace`, a non-safe method carries `Cavea-Csrf-Token`, and the member's role must grant the operation's `x-cavea-permission` (`x-cavea-roles` lists the roles that do). Every response carries `Cavea-Request-Id`; a caller may send its own (1 to 64 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -`). Errors are `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`: match on `code`, not on `message`. Lists are `{"data": [..], "next": <cursor or null>}`, oldest first; pass `next` back as `after`. The WebSocket protocol of `GET /v1/public/rt` is a binary protocol, which OpenAPI cannot describe.
info.title: Cavea server API

get.description: Newest first (the cursor is an entry's id): the workspace's sensitive actions, and the sign-ins, sign-outs and password changes of its current members.
Unexpired invitations of the workspace, oldest first; never a link.

post.description: With the token of an invitation link. Signed in (the cookie, with `Cavea-Csrf-Token`) as the invited email: joins the workspace. Not signed in, for an email with no account: `password` creates the user, who joins and is signed in. A wrong, expired or used token is `401` `invitation`; signed in as another email `403` `invitation_email`; an email that has an account, not signed in, `409` `sign_in`.

put.description: The file's text in `licence`. Only a user who owns every workspace on the server may (`403` `instance_owner`). A file that is not a licence signed by a key this build trusts is `400` `invalid_field` (`licence`) with `details.problem` saying why; nothing is stored. Otherwise it is stored for every node (each reads it within 30 s) and answered with the licence as `me` shows it; if `CAVEA_LICENCE` holds a better one, that one still counts. Works in every licence state.

get.description: The user, their workspaces and roles, the session's CSRF token.

post.description: Returns a one-time link for the email and role, shown only here (nothing is sent). It works once, for 7 days, and replaces any earlier invitation of the email to this workspace. Inviting an owner needs `ownership`. An email that is already a member's is `409`.

delete.description: Applies to the member's next request; the user and their other workspaces stay. Removing an owner needs `ownership`; the last owner cannot be removed.

patch.description: Applies to the member's next request. Making or unmaking an owner needs `ownership`; the last owner cannot be changed (`400`, `last_owner`).

post.description: A one-time link, shown only here (nothing is sent), that sets the member's password, for one hour; it replaces any earlier link for them. Using it ends every session of theirs; it clears their second factor only with `clear_second_factor`. The same rules as resetting a second factor.

delete.description: For someone who lost their authenticator: removes their secret and recovery codes; they sign in with the password alone and may enrol again. Resetting an owner needs `ownership`. The person must be one the caller may manage in every workspace they belong to (`403` `other_workspaces`), and not the caller (`403` `own_account`). Idempotent.

post.description: Ends every session of the user, this one included, and starts a new one. A wrong current password is `403` `credentials`.

With the token of a reset link and the new password. Ends every session of the user, then signs in (`200`), or answers `202` with the second step's challenge while the user has a second factor. A wrong, expired or used token is `401` `reset_token`.

delete.description: Ends the session on the server and clears the cookie.

post.description: A new session every time (any presented one is ended). A wrong email or password is `401` `credentials`, the same for both; repeated failures wait (`429`, `backoff`, `Retry-After`). A user with a second factor gets `202` and a `challenge` instead of a session, for `/console/api/session/second-factor`.

post.description: With the `challenge` of a sign-in that answered `202`, and a code from the authenticator app or an unused recovery code. A wrong code is `401` `second_factor` (after five, or once the challenge is used or five minutes old, `401` `challenge`: sign in again); repeated failures wait (`429`, `backoff`), as wrong passwords do.

Works while no user exists, once, with the token of the link the server logged at start-up (valid one hour; a restart makes a new one). The owner becomes owner of every workspace; with none, `workspace` (default `main`) is created. Signs the owner in. A wrong, expired or used token, or a server that has an owner, is `401` `setup_token`.
